items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015
items.q: then Duffy for a year, then Greg Fields was there for two years

ctx.x: Yeah. He was in a wheelchair. I think he’d had a stroke in about 1979 — 78 or 79. Butch was on the band at the time. And that was when I really became a fan of the band. When my teacher got the gig with the Basie band it was like whoa. So then I immersed myself in the Basie things. I bought all the old records like “April in Paris” and “Standing Ovation,” “Live at Birdland,” all of that stuff. “Atomic Basie.” And I just studied it and studied it. I had 95% of the book memorized when I got there.
Where did Duffy Jackson fit in that timeline?

There were four white drummers in a row. From Butch, who got the gig I think in ’75 through about ’79, then Duffy for a year, then Greg Fields was there for two years and then I was there for six months, and then Dennis Mackrel was after me. In 1983 he came after me. So I’m just honored to have my name in the list of people. It doesn’t matter that I didn’t record with them or that I didn’t do any extensive touring. It was all domestic.
